# Zero Trust Workload Identity Manager for Internal Service Authentication

Red Hat's Zero Trust Workload Identity Manager (ZTWIM) is an OpenShift operator built on
the CNCF-graduated SPIFFE/SPIRE project. It issues short-lived, cryptographically
attested identities to workloads — replacing static API keys, long-lived tokens, and
manual certificate management with automatic, workload-bound credentials that rotate
without human intervention.

ZTWIM reached general availability on January 23, 2026. It is bundled with OpenShift
Platform Plus, RHACM, and RHACS (no standalone purchase). It integrates with HashiCorp
Vault (secretless auth), Istio (mTLS mesh), Sigstore (supply chain), and OpenTelemetry
(secretless telemetry). An emerging use case is AI agent identity via the Kagenti
operator and A2A protocol.

## When to Use ZTWIM vs Alternatives

| Scenario | Recommendation |
|----------|---------------|
| Multi-cloud / hybrid with cross-cluster mTLS | **ZTWIM** — unified identity across environments |
| Compliance-mandated workload attestation | **ZTWIM** — cryptographic proof beyond K8s tokens |
| Eliminating static secrets from S2S auth | **ZTWIM** — automatic SVID rotation, Vault integration |
| AI agent identity for A2A communication | **ZTWIM + Kagenti** — early but promising |
| Single cluster, single cloud, K8s-only | **K8s bound SA tokens + cloud IAM** — simpler, sufficient |
| Tight delivery timeline (<6 months) | **Cloud-native identity** — ZTWIM takes 6-24 months |
| No cross-cluster communication needed | **Istio native or cert-manager** — less operational burden |

## Key Trade-offs

| Dimension | ZTWIM Strength | ZTWIM Cost |
|-----------|---------------|-----------|
| Security | Hardware-rooted attestation, short-lived certs | Operational complexity of SPIRE infrastructure |
| Scope | Single identity framework across all workload types | Requires OpenShift + Platform Plus subscription |
| Integration | Vault, Istio, Sigstore, OTEL composition | Each integration adds configuration surface |
| Scale | Proven at Uber (250K nodes) and Indeed (3K pods) | 1-3 dedicated engineers; 6-24 month deployment |
| Agent identity | JWS-signed Agent Cards with SPIFFE binding | A2A/MCP standards are early-stage |

## Quick Decision Checklist

1. Are workloads distributed across multiple clouds or on-prem + cloud? → Consider ZTWIM
2. Does your environment already run OpenShift with Platform Plus? → ZTWIM has zero licensing cost delta
3. Do compliance requirements mandate cryptographic workload attestation? → ZTWIM addresses this directly
4. Is the team willing to invest 6+ months in identity infrastructure? → ZTWIM requires this
5. Are you deploying AI agents that need runtime identity? → ZTWIM + Kagenti is the current Red Hat path

If answers to 1-3 are "no" and 4 is "no," simpler alternatives will serve better.
